fields.statement: Verifier at 77a481ff (attempt 2, fixing quality f1 / model f2). I read the diff: readyPick's dispatch.Load error now flows out of startWorkflowOfRef as an error, so runRunStart fails instead of falling back to ship-change. daemonUnresolvedReady now skips such a candidate as workflow-unresolved, with the load error in its detail, instead of keeping it for a default start. An explicit --workflow still never reads the file. I ran go test -trimpath ./internal/api with -run TestReadyWorkflowOrder (recorded over rule over ship-change), TestStartWorkflowExplicitWins (explicit over all), TestRunStartExplicitWorkflowOverRule, TestDaemonSkipsReadyWithUnresolvedWorkflow, TestDaemonSkipsReadyWithUnloadableDispatch (new), TestDaemonSkipsRequestWithUnresolvedWorkflow, TestDaemonStartsRequestWithDispatchedWorkflow and TestRunStartWorkflowRefusals: all PASS. The package's TestMain guard then reported .rhiza-root/usage.live.json changed. That file is the live root daemon's: it changed at 00:59:10 with no test running, so the report is environmental. The whole-package run hit Go's 600s timeout at VM load ~11, and CI's make check covers it. I ran go test -trimpath ./internal/dispatch/...: ok. I ran go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/(run-start-ready-dispatch|dispatch-check): both PASS. run-start-ready-dispatch shows run start --dry-run on a bug change set: with no dispatch file it falls to ship-change; with [ready] bug = "bugfix" it prints Workflow: bugfix; with --workflow other it prints other; with an unloadable dispatch.toml it fails naming dispatch.toml, not ship-change.
